learn.title: Doing math
learn.body: C has the operators you expect: `+` add, `-` subtract, `*` multiply, `/` divide. An operator combines values into a new value, so `3 + 4` has the value 7 and can be stored or printed.

learn.title: Order of operations
learn.body: Multiplication and division happen before addition and subtraction, just like in maths class. Use parentheses to choose the order yourself. Operators of equal rank work from left to right.

learn.title: Precedence at work
learn.body: The first line uses precedence, the second forces a different order.

learn.title: Shortcuts
learn.body: `x += 5` means `x = x + 5`. The same works for `-=`, `*=` and `/=`. `x++` adds 1 to `x`, and `x--` subtracts 1. These are very common, especially in loops, which come later.
If you are unsure about the order, add parentheses. They cost nothing and make code easier to read.

questions.explanation: Multiplication first: 3 * 4 is 12, and then 2 + 12 is 14.

questions.prompt: `int x = 10; x += 5;` What is `x`? Type the number.
`int x = 7; x++;` What is `x`? Type the number.

questions.explanation: The shortcut subtracts 3 from `x` and stores the result.
Equal-rank operators work left to right: 10 - 4 is 6, and then 6 - 3 is 3.

questions.prompt: Match each expression to its value.
questions.explanation: Work out the multiplication first unless parentheses say otherwise.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of `2 + 3 * 4 - 1` in order.
questions.explanation: Multiply first, then work the additions and subtractions from left to right.
